html:
The folk high school is a kind of school for adults, without exams, that began in Denmark at Rødding in 1844 on the ideas of the pastor and poet N. F. S. Grundtvig.

Grundtvig wanted schools that taught young farmers through the spoken word, song and Danish history, for life rather than for careers. After the defeat of 1864 the schools spread fast, and by 1900 a large share of young rural Danes had spent a winter at one.

The farmers they trained ran the cooperative dairies and slaughterhouses that made Danish butter and bacon famous, and sat in parliament. The movement spread to Norway, Sweden and Finland. It is one reason the Nordic countries put such weight on popular education and on the free farmers made by the end of the Stavnsbånd. See Denmark.
sum: The folk high school is a kind of school for adults, without exams, that began in Denmark at Rødding in 1844 on the ideas of the pastor and poet N. F. S. Grundtvig.
